newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-EVERTON TO WATCH COTE D'AZUR DERBY.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-EVERTON TO WATCH COTE D'AZUR DERBY.

text.p: Everton will be watching Monaco's Cote d'Azur derby at Nice on Wednesday, observing players on both sides in the clash between the top and bottom teams in the French first division.
The English premier league club want to see Monaco midfielder Laurent Viaud in action following his trial in Liverpool earlier this month.
They are also interested in Nice's talented Liberian international striker James Debbah.

Viaud has spent the better part of this season on the Monaco bench but looks set for a game as coach Jean Tigana rests one or two players following the exertions against Newcastle in the UEFA Cup last week and Bastia on Saturday.
"We have a difficult month to negotiate...but there is no question of taking this match against Nice lightly," Tigana said.
Monaco face Internazionale of Italy away on April 8 in the first leg of the semifinal and at home on April 22.
Midfielder Sylvain Legwinski said: "Nice are dangerous because in view of their position you run the risk of relaxing, of losing concentration.
"Let's not forget it's a derby and will be hard fought, our neighbours have nothing to lose and, on top of that, they have answers up front with James Debbah."
Defensive midfielder Gilles Grimandi recalled that Monaco had learned this season to treat all their matches with equal importance and that was at the heart of their success.
"In the past these were the kind of rendezvous that cost us dearest," he said.
Monaco beat Nice 4-1 when the two sides met in the principality in October.
